nodes.title: Exact equilibrium in polynomial time
nodes.summary: Shiva Kintali's November 24, 2026 preprint presents an exact polynomial-time algorithm on binary rational input. Lean verifies correctness of an executable solver following its sweep and quote search.
nodes.next: Complete the runtime refinement to the finite machine required by the public Lean statement.

nodes.title: Published results and algorithm
nodes.summary: Sources, baseline algorithms, and comparisons with later approaches.

nodes.title: Locate the exact algorithm and its worst-case bottleneck
nodes.summary: Identifies the published resource-augmentation algorithm and exhibits an edge that becomes active again.

nodes.title: Count strict threshold drops within one fixed-boundary phase
nodes.summary: Counting-network transportation margins force at least $2^h-1$ strict Algorithm 4 threshold drops on one fixed open boundary with $2h+2$ targets, unit losses, and two gains. The construction applies uniformly over the exact optimizing flows and fixed seed orders.

nodes.title: Account for exact arithmetic along a run
nodes.summary: Accounts for rational bit lengths, flow ties and non-repetition in the improved continuation upper bound.

nodes.title: Tighten the worst-case outer-call count on a single run
nodes.summary: With $n$ targets and $n$ positive-prior types, L1a forces $2^{\Omega(n)}$ outer calls, including on a single fixed-boundary phase. The exact implementation has an upper bound of $n^{O(n)}$ calls. The tight growth rate remains open.
nodes.next: Improve either bound using comparable dimensions, binary input sizes and tie rules. For a restricted class, identify the additional hypothesis.

nodes.title: Bound intermediate rational bit lengths by the original input size
nodes.summary: After j outer calls, L2 bounds the bit length of stored coordinates by a polynomial in the input length times j + 1. An input-only bound for the specified exact continuation remains open.
nodes.next: Bound the bit lengths of the reduced numerators and denominators of every retained coverage and flow by a polynomial in the original input length, or exhibit a family exceeding every such bound under specified optimizer choices.

nodes.title: Check the prior partial results and reconcile overlap
nodes.summary: Audits the supplied collection, records earlier results and isolates the exact market-oracle question.

nodes.title: Compare the Newton bound with the continuation landscape
nodes.summary: Transfers exact threshold endpoints from markets and tests the handicap-dependent Newton bound.
nodes.next: Use a general polynomial-time clearing method to make the threshold recovery unconditional.

nodes.title: Apply the handicap-dependent theorem to A4d
nodes.summary: The known A4d regularization can have exponential handicap in the binary input size.

nodes.title: Transfer market endpoints and exact threshold search to L1/L2
nodes.summary: An exact any-clearing oracle yields both threshold endpoints and permits budget search without tracing every flow change.

nodes.title: Worst-case run length by instance class
nodes.summary: Compares the longest run on one instance with the number of states reachable across a class.

nodes.title: Define a restricted Busy Beaver and test a state classification
nodes.summary: Bounds feasible payoff signatures and computes an exact longest-run example for independent blocks.

nodes.title: Combine independent preference components at one threshold
nodes.summary: Combines bounded-type preference components at a common threshold and one shared budget.

nodes.title: Bound progress with overlapping types
nodes.summary: Sparse cycles and a bounded set of slope generators give progress bounds. Dense slopes force many fixed-flow segments.
nodes.next: Find a tighter worst-case bound or a broader tractable class with a stated structural assumption.

nodes.title: Jump across steps that preserve an attack flow
nodes.summary: Extends coverage as far as possible at one attack flow and identifies a consumed cycle.

nodes.title: Count progress in closed reachable groups
nodes.summary: Bounds local cost levels inside closed groups with restricted slope and mass structure.

nodes.title: Search for long runs with exact arithmetic
nodes.summary: Exact small instances revisit old matching edges while their cost drops.

nodes.title: Compose groups that share targets
nodes.summary: One bounded shared target set admits composition across many groups.
nodes.next: Determine which budget and flow relations compose over a tree of small separators.

nodes.title: Embed a parametric path in one unchanged flow
nodes.summary: A parametric path gives many continuation changes even while one attack flow stays fixed.

nodes.title: Force many flow switches at uniform margins
nodes.summary: A second construction forces many different assignments on one run. The final budget of this family still admits a direct solver.

nodes.title: Independently check the forced-switch proof
nodes.summary: A separate model-assisted audit checks the forcing argument, binary sizes and the scope of the segment count.

nodes.title: Alternative exact algorithms
nodes.summary: Alternative equilibrium formulations and exact algorithms on restricted families.

nodes.title: Use payoff thresholds and capacitated transport
nodes.summary: Gives a threshold and transport certificate, exact face search, and weak-sign repair.

nodes.title: Solve the common-intercept class by logarithmic price changes
nodes.summary: Develops a log-price algorithm for a common-intercept payoff class.

nodes.title: Extend the log-price algorithm to arbitrary common offsets
nodes.summary: Extends the log-price argument to arbitrary common affine offsets with exact recovery.

nodes.title: Solve the binary-mass minimum-price market with arbitrary slopes
nodes.summary: A4i reduces general minimum-price search to one game equilibrium. Kintali's algorithm gives a polynomial-bit-time solver via that reduction.
nodes.next: Study direct market algorithms with arbitrary positive pair-specific slopes. Apply the [supply perturbation in A4c](A4c.md) to recover minimum prices from any clearing oracle.

nodes.title: Test contraction near factorized slopes
nodes.summary: Uses contraction to recover exact minimum prices when slopes are sufficiently near factorized.

nodes.title: Seek direct search through Hall inequalities
nodes.summary: Hall tests and elimination give polynomial algorithms for forests and bounded-deletion subclasses.

nodes.title: Reduce minimum-price search to any clearing equilibrium
nodes.summary: Any clearing equilibrium of one suitably enlarged market yields original minimum prices.

nodes.title: Reduce market and game equilibrium to P-matrix complementarity
nodes.summary: A single P-matrix LCP bounds the market and game search problems in UniqueEOPL.

nodes.title: Test covering LPs with reweighting and Hall cuts
nodes.summary: Reweighted covers descend exactly. A defect-one counting-network family forces superpolynomially many solves for the stated logarithmic tie-break, including with near-factorized slopes.

nodes.title: Identify when one weighted cover gives an unweighted flow
nodes.summary: An optimal weighted cover can have tight edges that fail the unweighted clearance test.

nodes.title: Test cuts across changing demand graphs
nodes.summary: A Hall obstruction can cease to apply when the price changes and the demand graph moves.

nodes.title: Prove strict descent and solve common-offset markets
nodes.summary: A secondary optimization yields strict descent. Common-offset markets have a separate polynomial solver.

nodes.title: Seek a polynomial-handicap formulation for A4d
nodes.summary: The existing scaling and reformulations do not give a uniform polynomial handicap bound.
nodes.next: Construct an equivalent bounded-handicap formulation with exact polynomial-time recovery.

nodes.title: Test scaling, regularization and active-set conditioning
nodes.summary: A small block preserves the handicap obstruction under positive diagonal scaling.

nodes.title: Construct equivalent buyer–good formulations
nodes.summary: Node formulations and supplied sign intervals expose better-conditioned restricted cells.
nodes.next: Find the right support or a global formulation in polynomial time.

nodes.title: Test bounded search and shortcuts in the implicit basis graph
nodes.summary: Bounded support search can verify a candidate exactly. Some natural search paths are long.
nodes.next: Give a complete polynomial-time choice of guesses or prove tractability for a wider class.

nodes.title: Solve selected affine regions and bracket their signs
nodes.summary: Selected affine regions can be solved and checked at exact prices.

nodes.title: Bound breadth-first and all-ones Lemke searches
nodes.summary: Ordinary breadth-first search and a specified Lemke line can visit many states.

nodes.title: Generate and search price lists from anchored paths
nodes.summary: Anchored paths supply exact price candidates and a Hall search uses complete lists.
nodes.next: Generate complete short lists without enumerating all anchored paths in a general market.

nodes.title: Generate complete candidate lists before the Hall search
nodes.summary: A4h5 obtains a singleton list via A4i and Kintali's algorithm. For direct affine-region search, polynomially many adaptive queries suffice in the abstract and selecting them efficiently remains open.
nodes.next: Give a polynomial-bit-time direct rule to choose the next affine region on an unrestricted supplied market.

nodes.title: Compose exact price breakpoints across one-good separators
nodes.summary: Separating blocks at one good permits adaptive breakpoint generation in several bounded classes.

nodes.title: Test fixed libraries and complete parametric tables
nodes.summary: Fixed formula libraries and explicit tables can need many entries.

nodes.title: Use contraction queries, load corrections, and price transforms
nodes.summary: Slope corrections and approximate common offsets give exact candidates for structured inputs.
nodes.next: Remove or weaken the normalization assumptions while retaining completeness.

nodes.title: Count capacity-price intervals and boundary-load drops
nodes.summary: Counting price plateaus across all capacities is NP-hard on the stated unit-slope inputs.

nodes.title: Generate complete candidates using the supplied capacities
nodes.summary: At supplied capacities, one call to Kintali's algorithm on the A4i game returns the exact minimum-price vector as a singleton candidate list in polynomial bit time.

nodes.title: Jump to new demand ties using alternating forests
nodes.summary: Alternating forests yield exact safe price jumps. Even a deficit of one can produce many internal events.
nodes.next: Bound a stronger shortcut on general inputs, or identify another class with polynomially many jumps.

nodes.title: Find and contract forced price relations
nodes.summary: A certified forced tie can be contracted while separate capacities and exact recovery are preserved.
nodes.next: Find enough forced relations in polynomial time without enumerating a large disjunction.

nodes.title: Preserve completions when discarding partial solutions
nodes.summary: At fixed boundary quotes one conditional price vector and joint flow set suffice. Committed boundary loads can form an exponential antichain.
nodes.next: Find the boundary prices and buyer utilities efficiently for broader separator classes.

nodes.title: Combine price jumps, certified ties, and boundary load queries
nodes.summary: A grouped solve tests price relations. Factorized cores with single-attachment branches admit polynomial-bit-time clearing. A projected Hall cut excludes a quote region after a failed joint test, even if private prices and demands change.
nodes.next: Find a polynomial-bit-time rule that combines projected Hall cuts and price-relation certificates to search independently quoted ports.

nodes.title: Reduce affine market clearing to one-resource security games
nodes.summary: One strictly signed game with one defender resource recovers exact affine-market minimum prices. Unit markets and games with uniform priors and equal gains are polynomial-time Turing equivalent.

nodes.title: Find the exact minimum prices of one supplied unit market
nodes.summary: Each buyer has unit mass and each good has unit capacity. Every offer can have its own positive rational slope.
nodes.next: Find a direct polynomial-bit-time market solver with arbitrary affine slopes and recover a clearing assignment. The degree-three reduction gives a sufficient restricted problem.

nodes.title: Complexity and counterexamples
nodes.summary: General complexity and counterexample directions.

nodes.title: Pin down compact complexity and certificate bounds
nodes.summary: The certificate and UniqueEOPL upper bounds leave the full complexity unresolved.
nodes.next: Strengthen a general upper or lower bound under the explicit rational encoding.

nodes.title: Test a structural conjecture or a candidate hardness reduction
nodes.summary: Threshold-zero selection and rent-division embeddings expose narrower hardness questions.
nodes.next: State a precise conjecture or reduction and show which exact equilibrium problem it addresses.

nodes.title: Use structure at one answer endpoint and test reusable price lists
nodes.summary: The supplied-budget search is polynomial if a recognizable hereditary market class applies at either specified answer endpoint. Failed class tests can guide threshold bisection.

nodes.title: Search synchronized boundary quotes and test persistent ties
nodes.summary: Certified synchronized quotes reduce a branch's joint boundary flow to a signed load for exact minimum-price search. Independent groups can be combined on a factorized core.

nodes.title: Combine common-offset cores and heterogeneous conditional solvers
nodes.summary: A rational piecewise-affine transformation solves a common-offset core of arbitrary slopes with tractable one-vertex branches. A final LP recovers the original prices.

nodes.title: Use one-good block solvers for shared buyers and goods
nodes.summary: A buyer proxy preserves clearance and turns the viable incidence graph into a goods-interaction graph. The existing block algorithm then handles arbitrary mixed articulations in bounded blocks.

nodes.title: Scale price precision with stable flows at physical quotas
nodes.summary: Dyadic contract phases recover exact minimum prices in polynomial bit time under a polynomial bound on products of slope ratios. Buyer masses and good capacities are binary rationals.

nodes.title: Solve degree-two unit markets by conditional Hall tests
nodes.summary: Degree two on either side admits polynomial-bit-time solving. Conditional Hall cuts and reciprocal transpose identities extend the result to additional balanced-cycle classes.

nodes.title: Bound exact ascent by deletion-matching products
nodes.summary: Cycle charging and allowed-edge decomposition give polynomial ascent on cactus graphs and under logarithmic local rank. A degree-three family forces superpolynomially many strict minimum-product drops on the deletion-matching ascent in every insertion order.

nodes.title: Reduce arbitrary unit markets to degree three
nodes.summary: One oracle call on a degree-three unit market recovers the original minimum. All heterogeneous offers can be placed on a matching between alternating paths.

nodes.title: Find support through multiplier lists and price boxes
nodes.summary: One representative per normalization choice covers the equilibria. A cut selects the lists for a fixed baseline, and a supplied price box can certify a matching or exclude an edge. Fixed cycle-gain rank yields another polynomial class.

nodes.title: Find exact clearing through ordinal stable allocation
nodes.summary: An edgewise separation test on two cutoff rankings gives exact polynomial-time clearing with binary masses and capacities. Supply enlargement recovers the minimum prices.

nodes.title: Transfer max-norm and lattice fixed-point algorithms to affine markets
nodes.summary: The pinned November preprint gives conditional polynomial bounds under an alternating-path LP or logarithmic vertex-cover size. The October solver gives exact subexponential search using vertex-cover elimination and direct integer flow recovery. The source audit records the scope of the imported statements.
nodes.next: Find a polynomial-time block search for the resulting integer maps or a polynomial-size max-norm formulation for general markets.
